title: Check yourself: The prefix, the breakpoint and the usage fields

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A response reports `cache_read_input_tokens` of 8,000, `cache_creation_input_tokens` of 0 and `input_tokens` of 40. How many input tokens did the request carry?

options.says: Ruled out because the sum "total_input_tokens = cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + input_tokens" has no subtraction.
Ruled out because the page sum adds a third term, and "total_input_tokens = cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + input_tokens" includes the 40.
Ruled out because that field holds only "tokens after the last breakpoint, which are not cached".
The page gives "total_input_tokens = cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + input_tokens", so 8,000 + 0 + 40.

questions.stem: A team marks a 1,500-token system prompt with `cache_control` on Claude Haiku 4.5 and sees both cache fields at 0, with no error. What explains it?

options.text: The text is under that model's 4,096 minimum, so it was handled as ordinary input
options.says: The page says "Any requests to cache fewer than this number of tokens will be processed without caching" and gives 4,096 for Claude Haiku 4.5.

options.text: The text is over that model's minimum, so the API is quietly returning stored answers
options.says: Ruled out because 1,500 is below the minimum, and "the prompt was not cached" is what two zeros mean.

options.text: The marker was ignored because system prompts are outside what the cache can hold
options.says: Ruled out because the page's hierarchy runs "up to and including the block designated with" the marker, and a system block can be that block.

options.text: The five-minute lifetime had lapsed before the first request was even sent
options.says: Ruled out because "Row 1 writes the 600 tokens" on a first request, so there is no earlier entry to lapse.

questions.stem: A request puts a block with the current clock reading ahead of a large stable policy, with the marker on the policy. Every call writes everything and never reads. Why?

options.text: The clock block counts as a second marker, which triggers a fresh write on each turn
options.says: Ruled out because "Explicit breakpoints put `cache_control` on individual blocks", and the clock block carries none, so it is no second marker.

options.text: The hash covers the marked block, so the policy is compared by itself and the clock is ignored
options.says: Ruled out because that same sentence says the key is "a hash of everything from the start of the request", not of one block.

options.text: All content before the boundary feeds the hash, so a changing line gives a new one
options.says: The page says "The cache key is a hash of everything from the start of the request up to the marked block", so a changing block before it gives a new key.

options.text: The hash is rebuilt from the user question, which differs on each turn of the chat
options.says: Ruled out because "Row 2, a minute later, reads them and pays for only the new question".
